newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - down sharply ahead of close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - down sharply ahead of close.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were sharply lower heading into the market's early close Thursday.
Traders said cash prices were off anywhere from 1/2 to 3/4 point in very light trading action.
Market participants said the problems began at mid-morning after a report on extremely strong home sales last month.
U.S. existing home sales surged nine percent to 4.26 million units, the second-highest rise on record. The figure exceeded the consensus estimate of 4.05 million units.
"They did not like this home sales number," one trader said. "There's not a lot of trading going on, but if you had to get a bid I would say it's probably off seven basis points" from Wednesday.

The government long bond also began falling after the number, and added to the losses after the key seven percent level broke. The long bond heading into the early 1400 EST close was down more than a point to 94-14/32 to yield 7.07 percent.
In the municipal secondary market, Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4 sewer bonds of 2027 dropped 1/2 point to 97.

Futures were also sharply lower heading into the early close, with the June municipal contract off 29/32 to 111-30/32 and June T-bonds off 1-1/32 to 107-14/32. The MOB spread widened to 144 ticks from 140 at the close on Wednesday.
Next week's supply is even lower than this week's relatively small figure, at about $1.5 billion.
Negotiated offerings total $1.3 billion in 40 sales, with a $231 million Delaware County, Pa., Industrial Development Authority deal through Goldman, Sachs & Co. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 33 sales totaling $210 million are on the schedule, a $29 million Broome County, N.Y., deal is the largest.
